cohort: 60 adult male patients with primary vaginal hydrocele were divided into two groups: one undergoing conventional hydrocelectomy and the other undergoing minimal access hydrocelectomy.
finding: Minimal access hydrocelectomy resulted in significantly shorter operating time (17.93 vs 30.83 minutes) and hospital stay (48.57 vs 80.50 hours), and fewer post-operative complications (edema, hardening, wound infection) compared to conventional hydrocelectomy.
